Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 60, verse 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

Tafsir of Surat al-Mumtahanah

It is Madinan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

The occasion of the revelation of the beginning of this noble surah [in (one manuscript): "the verse"; the text here follows the manuscripts M and A] was the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. Hatib was a man from the Muhajirun, and he was also among the people of Badr. He had children and property in Makkah, but he was not a member of the Quraysh themselves; rather, he was an ally [in A: "a guest"] of Uthman. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ resolved to conquer Makkah, because its people had broken the covenant, the Prophet ﷺ ordered the Muslims to prepare for their campaign and said: "O Allah, conceal our news from them." Hatib then deliberately wrote a letter and sent it with a woman of the Quraysh to the people of Makkah, informing them of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had resolved upon [regarding their campaign], so that he might thereby gain a favour with them. Allah informed His Messenger of this [in M: "Allah set right His Messenger concerning that"], in answer to his supplication. He then sent after the woman and took the letter from her. This is clearly stated in this hadith, whose authenticity is agreed upon. Imam Ahmad said:

Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr: Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali informed me: Ubayd Allah [in M: "Abd Allah"] ibn Abi Rafi' informed me — and Murrah said: Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi' informed him that he heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad, and said: "Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman riding a camel with a letter, so take it from her." So we set off, our horses galloping with us, until we reached the garden, and there was the woman. We said: "Bring out the letter." She said: "I have no letter." We said: "You will bring out the letter, or we will strip your garments." He said: She brought out the letter from her braid, and we took the letter and brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. In it was: "From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to some of the polytheists in Makkah, informing them of some of the matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Hatib, what is this?" He said: "Do not hasten against me. I was a man attached to the Quraysh, but I was not one of them by origin. Those of your companions who are Muhajirun all have relatives who protect their families in Makkah, so I wished, since I lacked that kinship among them, to make for myself a favour among them by which they would protect my relatives. I did not do this out of disbelief, nor apostasy from my religion, nor out of contentment with disbelief after Islam." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He has told you the truth." Umar said: "Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite." He said: "He has taken part in Badr. What would make you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you."

The Jama'ah all narrated this, except Ibn Majah, through several chains, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with this text. [Al-Musnad (1/79, 80); Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (3007, 4890); Sahih Muslim, no. (2494); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2650); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3305); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11585).] Al-Bukhari added in the Book of Campaigns: Then Allah revealed the surah: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4274)]. And in the Book of Tafsir he said: Amr said: It was revealed concerning him: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾. He said: "I do not know whether the verse is in the hadith or whether Amr said it." Al-Bukhari said: Ali (meaning Ibn al-Madini) said: It was said to Sufyan about this: "Was ﴿Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ revealed?" Sufyan said: "This is in the hadith of the people; I memorised it from Amr, I left out no letter of it, and I do not think anyone memorised it besides me." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4890).]

They both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs through the hadith of Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'd ibn Ubaydah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, Abu Marthad and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, and we were all mounted, and he said: "Set off until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman of the polytheists there with a letter from Hatib to the polytheists." We overtook her riding her camel just where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. We said: "The letter?" She said: "I have no letter." We made her kneel and searched, but we did not find a letter. We said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not lied, and neither have we!" "Either you bring out the letter, or we will strip you." When she saw the seriousness, she reached to her waistband, for she was wrapped in a cloak, and brought it out. We took her to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, he has betrayed Allah, His Messenger and the believers, so let me strike his neck." He said: "What led you to what you did?" He said: "By Allah, I am only a believer in Allah and His Messenger. I wished that there would be a favour for me among the people by which Allah would repel harm from my family and property, and none of your companions is without kinsmen there who protect his family and property through him." He said: "He has told the truth. Say to him only what is good." Umar said: "He has betrayed Allah, His Messenger and the believers, so let me strike his neck." He said: "Is he not one of the people of Badr?" He said: "Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you wish, for Paradise has become obligatory for you — or: I have forgiven you." The eyes of Umar filled with tears, and he said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3983); Sahih Muslim, no. (2494).]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari in the Book of Campaigns, in the Battle of Badr. It has also been narrated by another route from Ali. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hisnjani narrated to us: Ubayd ibn Ya'ish narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi narrated to us, from Abu Sinan (he is Sa'id ibn Sinan), from Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, from Abu al-Bakhtari al-Ta'i [in (one manuscript): "from Abu Ishaq al-Bakhtari al-Ta'i", the text here follows al-Tabari], from al-Harith, from Ali who said: When the Prophet ﷺ intended to go to Makkah, he confided to some people among his companions that he intended Makkah, among them Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, and he spread among the people that he intended Khaybar. He said: Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah wrote to the people of Makkah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was coming against them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was informed, and he sent me and Abu Marthad, and there was not a man among us who did not have a horse. He said: "Go to Rawdat Khakh, for you will meet a woman there with a letter, so take it from her." We set off until we saw her in the place the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had described. We said to her: "Bring the letter." She said: "I have no letter." We set down her baggage and searched her, but we did not find it among her belongings. Abu Marthad said: "Perhaps she does not have it with her." I said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not lied, nor have we." We said to her: "Either you bring it out, or we will expose you." She said: "Do you not fear Allah? Are you not Muslims?" We said: "Either you bring it out, or we will expose you." Amr ibn Murrah said: She brought it out from her waistband. Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: She brought it out from her private part. We brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and behold, the letter was from Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. Umar stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, he has betrayed Allah and His Messenger, so permit me to strike his neck." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Was he not present at Badr?" They said: "Yes." Umar said: "Yes, but he has broken faith and backed your enemies against you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you wish, for I see what you do." The eyes of Umar overflowed, and he said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Hatib and said: "O Hatib, what led you to what you did?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was a man attached to the Quraysh, and I had property and family there, and none of your companions was without someone in Makkah who protected his family and property. So I wrote to them about this. By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I am a believer in Allah and His Messenger." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hatib has told the truth, so say to Hatib only what is good." Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection﴾, the verse.

Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise, from Ibn Humayd, from Mihran, from Abu Sinan (Sa'id ibn Sinan), with its chain, the same. [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/38).] The people of the campaigns and biographies mentioned this. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in the Sirah:

Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others of our scholars, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ resolved on the march to Makkah, Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah wrote a letter to the Quraysh informing them of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had resolved upon concerning the march against them. Then he gave it to a woman — Muhammad ibn Ja'far claimed she was from Muzaynah, and others claimed she was Sarah, a freedwoman of the Banu Abd al-Muttalib — and he made for her a reward on condition that she deliver it to the Quraysh. She put it in her hair, then braided over it her locks, and went out with it. The news of what Hatib had done reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from heaven, so he sent Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and said: "Overtake a woman with whom Hatib has sent a letter to the Quraysh, warning them of what we have resolved upon regarding their affair."

The two set off until they overtook her at Khulaifah — Khulaifat Bani Abi Ahmad — and they made her dismount at Khulaifah. They searched her baggage but found nothing. Ali ibn Abi Talib said to her: "I swear by Allah that the Messenger of Allah has not lied, nor have we. Either you bring out this letter for us, or we will uncover you." When she saw the seriousness in him, she said: "Turn away." He turned away, and she untied the locks of her hair, drew out the letter from it, and handed it to him. He brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Hatib and said: "O Hatib, what led you to this?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I am a believer in Allah and His Messenger; I have not changed nor altered. But I was a man who had no kin or tribe among the people, and I had a son and family among them, so I courted them on their account." Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me strike his neck, for the man has become a hypocrite." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What would make you know, O Umar? Perhaps Allah looked upon the companions of Badr on the day of Badr and said: Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning Hatib: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection﴾, up to His saying: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people: Indeed, we are free from you and from what you worship other than Allah. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4], up to the end of the story. [Al-Tabari also narrated it in his tafsir (23/39) through the route of Abu Ishaq.]

Ma'mar related from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, something similar to that. Likewise Muqatil ibn Hayyan mentioned that these verses were revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah: that he sent Sarah, a freed slave-woman of the Banu Hashim, and that he gave her ten dirhams, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent after her 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them both, and they overtook her at al-Juhfah... He mentioned the complete story in a manner similar to what has preceded. And from al-Suddi, something close to it. Likewise al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others besides them that these verses were revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth﴾. That is, the polytheists and disbelievers who are at war with Allah, His Messenger and the believers, whose enmity and severance Allah has prescribed [in M: "prescribed for them"], and He forbade that they be taken as allies, friends and intimates, as He said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them is indeed one of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 51].

This is a severe threat and a firm warning. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you, nor the disbelievers, as allies. And fear Allah, if you should be believers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 57]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾ [al-Nisa': 144]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. And whoever does that has nothing with Allah, except when you fear from them a danger. And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ [Al 'Imran: 28]. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted the excuse of Hatib when he mentioned that he had only done that to gain favour with the Quraysh, because of the wealth and children he had among them.

Here is mentioned the hadith which Imam Ahmad related:

Musa'ab ibn Sallam narrated to us: al-Ajlah narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abi Muslim, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck for us examples: one, three, five, seven, nine and eleven. He said: He struck for us one of them and left the rest. He said: "Indeed a people were of weakness and humility, and they were fought by a people of tyranny and hostility. Allah made the weak prevail over them, but they went to their enemy, employed them and dominated them, so they angered Allah against them until the Day they meet Him."[[al-Musnad (5/407); and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/232): "In it is al-Ajlah al-Kindi, who is trustworthy but has been weakened, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They expel the Messenger and you﴾, this, together with what precedes it, is an incitement to enmity toward them and to not allying with them, because they expelled the Messenger and his Companions from among them, out of hatred for their monotheism and their sincere worship of Allah alone. For this reason He said: ﴿because you believe in Allah, your Lord﴾, meaning: you had no offence in their sight except your belief in Allah, the Lord of the worlds, as in His saying: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Buruj: 8], and as in His saying: ﴿who were expelled from their homes without right, only because they said, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ [al-Hajj: 40].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿if you have gone out to strive in My cause and seeking My approval﴾, that is: if you are such, then do not take them as allies. If you have gone out as fighters in My way, seeking My approval for you, then do not ally with My enemies and your enemies, while they have expelled you from your homes and your wealth out of rage against you and anger at your religion.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You confide to them affection, and I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare﴾, that is: you do that while I am the Knower of secrets, inner thoughts and outward matters. ﴿And whoever of you does it has certainly strayed from the sound way. If they overcome you, they will be enemies to you and extend against you their hands and their tongues with evil﴾, that is: if they were able over you, they would not refrain from harming you by word and deed. ﴿And they wish you would disbelieve﴾, that is: they are eager that you should not attain any good. So their enmity toward you is both hidden and apparent. How then would you ally with such as these? This is also an incitement against their enmity.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you. And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, that is: your kinship will not benefit you with Allah if He intends harm for you, and their benefit will not reach you if you please them with what angers Allah. Whoever agrees with his family in disbelief to please them has indeed lost, failed and his deed has gone astray, and his kinship to anyone will not benefit him with Allah, even if he were close to one of the prophets. Imam Ahmad said:

'Affan narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, where is my father?" He said: "In the Fire." When he turned to leave, he called him back and said: "Indeed my father and your father are in the Fire."

Muslim and Abu Dawud related it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording.[[al-Musnad (3/268); Sahih Muslim no. (203); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (8174).]]

Allah says to His believing servants, whom He commanded to cut off from the disbelievers, to be hostile to them, to keep away from them, and to disassociate themselves from them:

"There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him" — i.e., and his followers who believed with him — "when they said to their people, 'Indeed, we are disassociated from you'" — i.e., we have disowned you — "'and from that which you worship other than Allah, we have rejected you'" — i.e., your religion and your way — "'and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever'" — meaning: enmity and hatred have been prescribed between us and you from now on, as long as you remain upon your disbelief. So we will forever disown you and hate you — "'until you believe in Allah alone'" — i.e., until you affirm the oneness of Allah, worship Him alone without partner, and cast off what you worship besides Him of rivals and idols.

* *

And the request of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was compassionate and forbearing" (At-Tawbah: 113–114). He joins hearts after enmity and hardness, so that they become united and in agreement. As God, exalted is He, said, bestowing favour upon the Ansar: ﴿And remember the favour of God upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, and you became, by His favour, brothers. [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 1997, by way of Suwayd ibn 'Amr, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet. End of the note as drawn from the margin of the Ta-Sha'b edition.]:

*"God may bring together the two scattered ones after they had thought, with complete certainty, that they would never meet."*

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, He forgives the disbelievers their disbelief when they repent from it, turn back in repentance to their Lord, and submit to Him. He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, to everyone who turns to Him in repentance, whatever sin it may be.

It was read to Muhammad ibn 'Aziz: Salamah narrated to me, 'Uqayl narrated to me, Ibn Shihab narrated to me, that the Messenger of God ﷺ appointed Abu Sufyan ibn Harb over part of Yemen. When the Messenger of God ﷺ passed away, he set out and met Dhu al-Khimar, who had apostatised, and he fought him. He was the first to fight in the Ridda and to strive in defence of the religion. Ibn Shihab said: He is among those concerning whom God revealed: ﴿It may be that God will bring about affection between you and those among them with whom you have been at enmity. In Sahih Muslim, from Ibn 'Abbas: Abu Sufyan said: "O Messenger of God, give me three things." He said: "Yes." He said: "And will you appoint me to fight the disbelievers as I used to fight the Muslims?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And will you make Mu'awiyah your scribe in your presence?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And I have the most beautiful and handsome of the Arabs, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan; I will marry her to you..." and the hadith continues. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2501, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him. The statement of the Hafiz, "The discussion of it has already passed," I do not know what he intends by it, for he mentioned the hadith when commenting on verse 227 of Surah al-Shu'ara' and said nothing about it. It may be that he discussed it in another place that I have not come across, and God knows best. The hadith has been found problematic: Abu Sufyan's statement in the hadith, "I have Umm Habibah whom I will marry to you," is refuted by the fact that Abu Sufyan embraced Islam only on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, while the Prophet ﷺ had married Umm Habibah long before that. See the words of Imam al-Nawawi in al-Minhaj (16/63) and his answer to this.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Asma' (she is the daughter of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with both of them), who said: My mother came to me while she was a polytheist, during the period of the treaty of the Quraysh when they made their covenant. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, my mother has come to me and she desires (my help). Shall I maintain ties with her?" He said: "Yes, maintain ties with your mother." [Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim.] [The hadith has reached me by a route other than this one. See: al-Musnad (6/344, 347); Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2620, 3183, 5978; Sahih Muslim, no. 1003.]

And Imam Ahmad said: 'Arim narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit narrated to us, 'Amir ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from his father, who said: Qutaylah came to her daughter Asma' bint Abi Bakr with gifts: sinab, aqit, and ghee, while she was a polytheist. Asma' refused to accept her gift and to let her enter her house. So 'A'ishah asked the Prophet ﷺ, and God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion...﴾ to the end of the verse. He then commanded her to accept her gift and to let her into her house.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it in the same way, from the hadith of Mus'ab ibn Thabit. [al-Musnad (4/4) and Tafsir al-Tabari (28/43).] In a narration of Ahmad and Ibn Jarir: "Qutaylah bint 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn [Abd] As'ad, of the Banu Malik ibn Hasal." [Added from Musnad Imam Ahmad.] (In another version: "Qabilah bint al-'Uzzi ibn Sa'd, of the Banu Malik ibn Hanbal.") Ibn Abi Hatim added: "During the period of truce that existed between the Quraysh and the Messenger of God ﷺ."

Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said: 'Abdullah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Qatadah al-'Adawi narrated to us, from the nephew of al-Zuhri, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah and Asma', that they both said: Our mother came to us in Medina while she was a polytheist, during the truce that existed between the Quraysh and the Messenger of God ﷺ. We said: "O Messenger of God, our mother has come to us in Medina, desiring (our help). Shall we maintain ties with her?" He said: "Yes, maintain ties with her." [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 1873 (Kashf al-Astar). Al-Haythami said: "The hadith of Asma' is in the Sahih, and the mother of 'A'ishah is not the mother of Asma'." Then he said: "We do not know this hadith to be narrated from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, except by this route."

I say: It is munkar in this form, because the mother of 'A'ishah is Umm Ruman, and she was a Muslim emigrant, and the mother of Asma' is someone else, as is explicitly stated by name in the earlier hadiths. And God knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 60, verse 10–11 (part 1 of 2):

The account of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (sulh al-Hudaybiyyah), which took place between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the disbelievers of Quraysh, has already been mentioned in Surah al-Fath. In it was the stipulation: "That no man will come to you from us, even if he is upon your religion, except that you will return him to us." And in another narration: "That no one will come to you from us, even if he is upon your religion, except that you will return him to us." This is the view of Urwah, al-Dahhak, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, al-Zuhri, Muqatil, and al-Suddi. According to this narration, this verse is a specification (takhsis) of the Sunnah, and this is one of the best examples of that. According to the approach of some of the early scholars (al-salaf), it abrogates (nasikhah) it. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded His believing servants that when women come to them as emigrants (muhajirat), they should test them, and if they know them to be believers, they should not return them to the disbelievers: "They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them (the disbelievers)."

We have mentioned in the biography of Abd Allah ibn Abi Ahmad ibn Jahsh, from the Musnad al-Kabir, through the route of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Asim, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli, from Yaqub ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran, from Mujamma' ibn Ya'qub, from Husayn ibn Abi Lubana, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ahmad, who said: Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt emigrated during the emigration, and her two brothers, Umarah and al-Walid, set out until they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him about her, asking that he return her to them. So Allah annulled the covenant between him and the polytheists concerning women specifically, prohibited that they be returned to the polytheists, and Allah revealed the verse of the testing (ayat al-imtihan) [[Jami' al-masanid wa al-sunan li Ibn Kathir (7/243), and Ibn al-Athir narrated it in Usd al-Ghabah (3/67) through the route of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Asim; Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran is weak.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-Aghharr ibn al-Sabbah, from Khalifah, from Husayn, from Abu Nasr al-Asadi, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked: How did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) test the women? He said: He would test them: "By Allah, did you not leave out of hatred for a husband? By Allah, did you not leave out seeking to turn away from one land to another? By Allah, did you not leave out seeking worldly gain? By Allah, did you not leave out only out of love for Allah and His Messenger?" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/44).]]

Then he narrated it from another route, from al-Aghharr ibn al-Sabbah, with the same chain. Likewise al-Bazzar narrated it through the same route, and he mentioned in it that the one who would administer the oath to them, by the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was Umar ibn al-Khattab [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2272), Kashf al-Astar, and he said: "We do not know it being narrated from Ibn Abbas except by this chain, nor narrated from Abu Nasr except by Khalifah." al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/123): "In it is Qays ibn al-Rabi', whom Shu'bah and al-Thawri declared trustworthy, while others declared him weak, and the rest of its narrators are reliable." Ibn Hajar criticized this in Mukhtasar al-Zawa'id (1/112). I say: the shaykh (al-Haythami) gave as its defect Qays, and al-Bukhari mentioned that Abu Nasr did not hear from Ibn Abbas, so that is the defect.]].

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: "O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them" that their testing was that they bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and that Muhammad is the servant of Allah [[In manuscript M: "and that Muhammad is His servant."]] and His Messenger.

Mujahid said: "Then test them" means: ask them why they have come. If they have anger against their husbands, or resentment, or something else, and they are not believers, then return them to their husbands.

Ikrimah said: It is said to her: "What brought you except love of Allah and His Messenger? And what brought you not the passion for a man among us, nor flight from your husband?" That is the meaning of His statement: "Then test them."

Qatadah said: Their testing was that they be made to swear by Allah: "What drove you out, rebelliousness? And what drove you out except love of Islam and its people, and eagerness for it?" When they say that, it is accepted from them.

* *

His statement: "If you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers" contains evidence that faith can be known with certainty.

* *

His statement: "They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them" — this verse is what made believing women unlawful for polytheists. It had been permissible in the early period of Islam for a polytheist man to marry a believing woman. For this reason, Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', husband of the Prophet's daughter Zaynab (may Allah be pleased with her), was upon the religion of his people while she was a Muslim. When he was taken captive on the day of Badr, his wife Zaynab sent, for his ransom, a necklace that had belonged to her mother Khadijah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw it, he was moved by it with intense tenderness, and he said to the Muslims: "If you see fit to release her captive for her, then do so." They did so, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) released him on condition that he send his daughter to him. He fulfilled that for him and was truthful regarding what he had promised, and sent her to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with Zayd ibn Harithah (may Allah be pleased with him). She remained in Medina from after the battle of Badr, which was in the second year, until her husband al-As ibn al-Rabi' embraced Islam in the eighth year, and he returned her to him with the first marriage contract, and he did not establish a new dowry for her, as Imam Ahmad said:

Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned his daughter Zaynab to Abu al-As [ibn al-Rabi'] [[Addition from Musnad al-Imam Ahmad.]], and her emigration had been six years before his embracing Islam, on the first marriage contract, and he did not establish a new testimony nor a dowry.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also narrated it [[Al-Musnad (1/261), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2240), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1143), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2009).]]. Some say "after two years," and this is sound, because his embracing Islam was two years after the prohibition of Muslim women to polytheists. al-Tirmidhi said: "There is nothing wrong with its chain, but we do not know the basis of this hadith, and perhaps it came from the memorization of Dawud ibn al-Husayn. I heard Abd ibn Humayd say: I heard Yazid ibn Harun mention from Ibn Ishaq this hadith, and the hadith of Ibn al-Hajjaj — meaning Ibn Artat — from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned his daughter to Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi' with a new dowry and a new marriage contract." Yazid said: "The hadith of Ibn Abbas is better in chain, and practice is according to the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb."

I say: The hadith of al-Hajjaj ibn Artat from Amr ibn Shu'ayb has been narrated by Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah [[Al-Musnad (2/207), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1142), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2010).]], and Imam Ahmad and others declared it weak, and Allah knows best.

The majority answered the hadith of Ibn Abbas by saying that this was a specific case (qadiyyat 'ayn), and it is possible that her waiting period (iddah) had not expired from him; for the view of most scholars is that when the waiting period has expired and he has not embraced Islam, her marriage to him is annulled.

Others said: rather, when the waiting period has expired, she has the choice: if she wishes, she may remain in the marriage and continue, and if she wishes, she may annul it and go off and marry. They applied the hadith of Ibn Abbas to this, and Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: "And give them what they have spent" — meaning: the husbands of the emigrant women from among the polytheists. Pay them what they paid out for them of the dowries. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, and others.

* *

His statement: "And there is no blame upon you for marrying them when you have given them their due compensation" — meaning: when you give them their dowries, then marry them, that is, marry them on its condition, from the completion of the waiting period, the guardian (wali), and other than that.

* *

His statement: "And do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women" — this is a prohibition from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon His believing servants against marrying polytheist women and continuing with them.

In the Sahih, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from al-Miswar and Marwan ibn al-Hakam: that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant with the disbelievers of Quraysh on the day of Hudaybiyyah, believing women came, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants [then test them]" up to His statement: "and do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women." So Umar ibn al-Khattab divorced two wives that day: one of them Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married, and the other Safwan ibn Umayyah [[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (2731, 2732).]].

Ibn Thawr narrated from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: This verse was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was at the lower part of Hudaybiyyah, when he made peace with them on the basis that whoever came to him from them he would return to them. When women came to him, this verse was revealed, and he was commanded to return the dowry to their husbands, and he ruled the same concerning the polytheists: if a Muslim woman came to them, they should return the dowry to her husband. And [Allah] said: "And do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women." Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise, and said: Allah only judged between them in this manner because of the covenant that existed between them and them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from al-Zuhri: Umar divorced on that day Qurayba bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, and Mu'awiyah married her; and Umm Kulthum bint Amr ibn Jarwal al-Khuza'iyyah, who was the mother of Ubayd Allah, and Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah ibn Ghanim, a man from her people, married her, and they were both upon their polytheism; and Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah divorced Arwa bint Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and after him Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-As married her [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/47), with slight variation.]].

* *

His statement: "And ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent" — meaning: demand from them what you spent upon your wives who go to the disbelievers, if they go; and let them demand what they spent upon their wives who emigrated to the Muslims.

* *

His statement: "That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you" — meaning: concerning the treaty and the exception of women from it. The command of all this is the judgment of Allah by which He judges among His creation: "And Allah is Knowing, Wise" — meaning, Knowing of what sets right His servants, Wise in that.

Then He said: "And if any of your wives have gone from you to the disbelievers and you had a retaliation (fa'aqabtum), then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent" [Qur'an 60:11]. Mujahid and Qatadah said: This applies to the disbelievers who have no covenant: when a woman flees to them and they do not give her husband anything, then when a woman comes from them, nothing is given to her husband until they give to the husband of the one who went to them an amount equal to his expenditure upon her.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Yunus informed me, from al-Zuhri, who said: The believers acknowledged the judgment of God, so they paid what they had been commanded to pay of the expenses of the polytheists' wives, which the polytheists had spent on them. But the polytheists refused to acknowledge God's judgment regarding what He had enjoined upon them of paying the expenses of the Muslims. So God said to the believers concerning this: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you then have a turn of victory, give those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent﴾ and fear God, in whom you believe. Then, if after this verse a woman from the wives of the believers had gone over to the polytheists, the believers would return to her husband the expenses he had spent on her from the spoils (al-'aqib) in their hands, which they had been commanded to return to the polytheists from their expenses that they had spent on their wives, who had believed and emigrated. Then they would return to the polytheists any surplus, if any remained for them. Al-'Aqib is what was in the hands of the believers of the dowries of the wives of the disbelievers when they believed and emigrated.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: its meaning is that if the wife of a man among the emigrants joined the disbelievers, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ordered that he be given from the spoils the like of what he had spent.

Similarly Mujahid said: ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ means you obtained booty from the Quraysh or others. ﴿Give those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent﴾ means: the bridal gift of their like (mahr mithlaha). Similarly said Masruq, Ibrahim, Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Dahhak, Sufyan ibn Husayn, and also al-Zuhri.

This does not contradict the first view, for if the first is possible, it is preferable; otherwise it is from the spoils taken from the hands of the disbelievers. This is broader, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. And to God belongs all praise and grace.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 60, verse 10–11 (part 1 of 2):

The account of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (sulh al-Hudaybiyyah), which took place between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the disbelievers of Quraysh, has already been mentioned in Surah al-Fath. In it was the stipulation: "That no man will come to you from us, even if he is upon your religion, except that you will return him to us." And in another narration: "That no one will come to you from us, even if he is upon your religion, except that you will return him to us." This is the view of Urwah, al-Dahhak, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, al-Zuhri, Muqatil, and al-Suddi. According to this narration, this verse is a specification (takhsis) of the Sunnah, and this is one of the best examples of that. According to the approach of some of the early scholars (al-salaf), it abrogates (nasikhah) it. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded His believing servants that when women come to them as emigrants (muhajirat), they should test them, and if they know them to be believers, they should not return them to the disbelievers: "They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them (the disbelievers)."

We have mentioned in the biography of Abd Allah ibn Abi Ahmad ibn Jahsh, from the Musnad al-Kabir, through the route of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Asim, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli, from Yaqub ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran, from Mujamma' ibn Ya'qub, from Husayn ibn Abi Lubana, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ahmad, who said: Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt emigrated during the emigration, and her two brothers, Umarah and al-Walid, set out until they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him about her, asking that he return her to them. So Allah annulled the covenant between him and the polytheists concerning women specifically, prohibited that they be returned to the polytheists, and Allah revealed the verse of the testing (ayat al-imtihan) [[Jami' al-masanid wa al-sunan li Ibn Kathir (7/243), and Ibn al-Athir narrated it in Usd al-Ghabah (3/67) through the route of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Asim; Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran is weak.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-Aghharr ibn al-Sabbah, from Khalifah, from Husayn, from Abu Nasr al-Asadi, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked: How did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) test the women? He said: He would test them: "By Allah, did you not leave out of hatred for a husband? By Allah, did you not leave out seeking to turn away from one land to another? By Allah, did you not leave out seeking worldly gain? By Allah, did you not leave out only out of love for Allah and His Messenger?" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/44).]]

Then he narrated it from another route, from al-Aghharr ibn al-Sabbah, with the same chain. Likewise al-Bazzar narrated it through the same route, and he mentioned in it that the one who would administer the oath to them, by the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was Umar ibn al-Khattab [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2272), Kashf al-Astar, and he said: "We do not know it being narrated from Ibn Abbas except by this chain, nor narrated from Abu Nasr except by Khalifah." al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/123): "In it is Qays ibn al-Rabi', whom Shu'bah and al-Thawri declared trustworthy, while others declared him weak, and the rest of its narrators are reliable." Ibn Hajar criticized this in Mukhtasar al-Zawa'id (1/112). I say: the shaykh (al-Haythami) gave as its defect Qays, and al-Bukhari mentioned that Abu Nasr did not hear from Ibn Abbas, so that is the defect.]].

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: "O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them" that their testing was that they bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and that Muhammad is the servant of Allah [[In manuscript M: "and that Muhammad is His servant."]] and His Messenger.

Mujahid said: "Then test them" means: ask them why they have come. If they have anger against their husbands, or resentment, or something else, and they are not believers, then return them to their husbands.

Ikrimah said: It is said to her: "What brought you except love of Allah and His Messenger? And what brought you not the passion for a man among us, nor flight from your husband?" That is the meaning of His statement: "Then test them."

Qatadah said: Their testing was that they be made to swear by Allah: "What drove you out, rebelliousness? And what drove you out except love of Islam and its people, and eagerness for it?" When they say that, it is accepted from them.

* *

His statement: "If you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers" contains evidence that faith can be known with certainty.

* *

His statement: "They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them" — this verse is what made believing women unlawful for polytheists. It had been permissible in the early period of Islam for a polytheist man to marry a believing woman. For this reason, Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', husband of the Prophet's daughter Zaynab (may Allah be pleased with her), was upon the religion of his people while she was a Muslim. When he was taken captive on the day of Badr, his wife Zaynab sent, for his ransom, a necklace that had belonged to her mother Khadijah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw it, he was moved by it with intense tenderness, and he said to the Muslims: "If you see fit to release her captive for her, then do so." They did so, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) released him on condition that he send his daughter to him. He fulfilled that for him and was truthful regarding what he had promised, and sent her to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with Zayd ibn Harithah (may Allah be pleased with him). She remained in Medina from after the battle of Badr, which was in the second year, until her husband al-As ibn al-Rabi' embraced Islam in the eighth year, and he returned her to him with the first marriage contract, and he did not establish a new dowry for her, as Imam Ahmad said:

Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned his daughter Zaynab to Abu al-As [ibn al-Rabi'] [[Addition from Musnad al-Imam Ahmad.]], and her emigration had been six years before his embracing Islam, on the first marriage contract, and he did not establish a new testimony nor a dowry.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also narrated it [[Al-Musnad (1/261), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2240), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1143), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2009).]]. Some say "after two years," and this is sound, because his embracing Islam was two years after the prohibition of Muslim women to polytheists. al-Tirmidhi said: "There is nothing wrong with its chain, but we do not know the basis of this hadith, and perhaps it came from the memorization of Dawud ibn al-Husayn. I heard Abd ibn Humayd say: I heard Yazid ibn Harun mention from Ibn Ishaq this hadith, and the hadith of Ibn al-Hajjaj — meaning Ibn Artat — from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned his daughter to Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi' with a new dowry and a new marriage contract." Yazid said: "The hadith of Ibn Abbas is better in chain, and practice is according to the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb."

I say: The hadith of al-Hajjaj ibn Artat from Amr ibn Shu'ayb has been narrated by Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah [[Al-Musnad (2/207), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1142), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2010).]], and Imam Ahmad and others declared it weak, and Allah knows best.

The majority answered the hadith of Ibn Abbas by saying that this was a specific case (qadiyyat 'ayn), and it is possible that her waiting period (iddah) had not expired from him; for the view of most scholars is that when the waiting period has expired and he has not embraced Islam, her marriage to him is annulled.

Others said: rather, when the waiting period has expired, she has the choice: if she wishes, she may remain in the marriage and continue, and if she wishes, she may annul it and go off and marry. They applied the hadith of Ibn Abbas to this, and Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: "And give them what they have spent" — meaning: the husbands of the emigrant women from among the polytheists. Pay them what they paid out for them of the dowries. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, and others.

* *

His statement: "And there is no blame upon you for marrying them when you have given them their due compensation" — meaning: when you give them their dowries, then marry them, that is, marry them on its condition, from the completion of the waiting period, the guardian (wali), and other than that.

* *

His statement: "And do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women" — this is a prohibition from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon His believing servants against marrying polytheist women and continuing with them.

In the Sahih, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from al-Miswar and Marwan ibn al-Hakam: that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant with the disbelievers of Quraysh on the day of Hudaybiyyah, believing women came, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants [then test them]" up to His statement: "and do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women." So Umar ibn al-Khattab divorced two wives that day: one of them Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married, and the other Safwan ibn Umayyah [[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (2731, 2732).]].

Ibn Thawr narrated from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: This verse was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was at the lower part of Hudaybiyyah, when he made peace with them on the basis that whoever came to him from them he would return to them. When women came to him, this verse was revealed, and he was commanded to return the dowry to their husbands, and he ruled the same concerning the polytheists: if a Muslim woman came to them, they should return the dowry to her husband. And [Allah] said: "And do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women." Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise, and said: Allah only judged between them in this manner because of the covenant that existed between them and them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from al-Zuhri: Umar divorced on that day Qurayba bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, and Mu'awiyah married her; and Umm Kulthum bint Amr ibn Jarwal al-Khuza'iyyah, who was the mother of Ubayd Allah, and Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah ibn Ghanim, a man from her people, married her, and they were both upon their polytheism; and Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah divorced Arwa bint Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and after him Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-As married her [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/47), with slight variation.]].

* *

His statement: "And ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent" — meaning: demand from them what you spent upon your wives who go to the disbelievers, if they go; and let them demand what they spent upon their wives who emigrated to the Muslims.

* *

His statement: "That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you" — meaning: concerning the treaty and the exception of women from it. The command of all this is the judgment of Allah by which He judges among His creation: "And Allah is Knowing, Wise" — meaning, Knowing of what sets right His servants, Wise in that.

Then He said: "And if any of your wives have gone from you to the disbelievers and you had a retaliation (fa'aqabtum), then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent" [Qur'an 60:11]. Mujahid and Qatadah said: This applies to the disbelievers who have no covenant: when a woman flees to them and they do not give her husband anything, then when a woman comes from them, nothing is given to her husband until they give to the husband of the one who went to them an amount equal to his expenditure upon her.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Yunus informed me, from al-Zuhri, who said: The believers acknowledged the judgment of God, so they paid what they had been commanded to pay of the expenses of the polytheists' wives, which the polytheists had spent on them. But the polytheists refused to acknowledge God's judgment regarding what He had enjoined upon them of paying the expenses of the Muslims. So God said to the believers concerning this: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you then have a turn of victory, give those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent﴾ and fear God, in whom you believe. Then, if after this verse a woman from the wives of the believers had gone over to the polytheists, the believers would return to her husband the expenses he had spent on her from the spoils (al-'aqib) in their hands, which they had been commanded to return to the polytheists from their expenses that they had spent on their wives, who had believed and emigrated. Then they would return to the polytheists any surplus, if any remained for them. Al-'Aqib is what was in the hands of the believers of the dowries of the wives of the disbelievers when they believed and emigrated.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: its meaning is that if the wife of a man among the emigrants joined the disbelievers, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ordered that he be given from the spoils the like of what he had spent.

Similarly Mujahid said: ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ means you obtained booty from the Quraysh or others. ﴿Give those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent﴾ means: the bridal gift of their like (mahr mithlaha). Similarly said Masruq, Ibrahim, Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Dahhak, Sufyan ibn Husayn, and also al-Zuhri.

This does not contradict the first view, for if the first is possible, it is preferable; otherwise it is from the spoils taken from the hands of the disbelievers. This is broader, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. And to God belongs all praise and grace.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 60, verse 12 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn Akhi Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from his paternal uncle, who said: 'Urwah informed me that 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to test the believing women who emigrated to him with this verse: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you...﴾ up to his words ﴿...Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ 'Urwah said: 'A'ishah said: "When a believing woman acknowledged this condition, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say to her: 'I have accepted your pledge,' only verbally. By Allah, his hand never touched the hand of any woman in the pledging. He would accept their pledge only with his words: 'I have accepted your pledge regarding that.'" This is the wording of al-Bukhari.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4891). In the narration of Abu Dharr: "Ishaq narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us."]]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umaymah bint Ruqayqah, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with some women to pledge allegiance to him. He took our pledge concerning what is in the Qur'an: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾ the verse, and he said: 'In what you are able and capable of.' We said: 'Allah and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will you not shake hands with us?' He said: 'I do not shake hands with women. My word to one woman is like my word to a hundred women.'"[[In manuscript M: "I came to the Prophet."]][[In manuscript M: "one woman of you."]]

This is a ṣaḥīḥ (authentic) chain of narration (isnad). It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah (and al-Nasa'i also through al-Thawri) and Malik ibn Anas, all of them from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir with the same wording.[[Musnad (6/357); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1597); Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/149); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2874).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan ṣaḥīḥ (good and authentic). We do not know it except through the narration of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir."

Ahmad also related it through Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umaymah, with the addition: "He did not shake hands with any of us women."[[Musnad (6/357).]] Likewise, Ibn Jarir related it through the route of Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, with the same wording.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/53).]] Ibn Abi Hatim related it from the narration of Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir: "Umaymah bint Ruqayqah narrated to me, and she was the sister of Khadijah, the maternal aunt of Fatimah, directly from her mouth to mine," and he mentioned it.

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, Salit ibn Ayyub ibn al-Hakam ibn Sulaym narrated to me, from his mother Salma bint Qays, who was one of the maternal aunts of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who had prayed with him facing both qiblahs, and who was one of the women of Bani 'Adi ibn al-Najjar. She said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to pledge allegiance to him among women of the Ansar. When he stipulated to us: that we would not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor bring a slander that we fabricate between our hands and feet, nor disobey him in what is right," he said: "And that you will not deceive your husbands." She said: "So we pledged allegiance to him, then we left. I said to one of them: 'Go back and ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: what is the deceiving of our husbands?' She asked him, and he said: 'That she takes his property and gives it to another.'"[[Musnad (6/379).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-'Abbas narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Hatib narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his mother 'A'ishah bint Qudamah, that is, the daughter of Maz'un, who said: "I was with my mother Ra'itah bint Sufyan al-Khuza'iyyah, while the Prophet ﷺ was pledging allegiance to the women, saying: 'I pledge allegiance to you that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your children, nor bring a slander that you fabricate between your hands and feet, nor disobey me in what is right.' [She said: They lowered their heads. Then the Prophet ﷺ said to them] [[Addition from Musnad Imam Ahmad.]] They said: 'Yes, in what you are able to do.' So they would say it, and I would say it with them, while my mother was prompting me: 'Say it, my daughter: yes, in what I am able to do.' So I would say as they said."[[Musnad (6/365).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu Ma'mar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from Umm 'Atiyyah, who said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he recited to us: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾ and forbade us from wailing (niyahah). A woman withdrew her hand and said: 'Such-and-such a woman gave me support, and I want to repay her.' The Prophet ﷺ said nothing to her. She left and then came back, and he pledged allegiance to her."

Muslim also related it.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4892); Sahih Muslim, no. (936).]] In one narration: "None of them fulfilled it except her, and Umm Sulaym bint Milhan."

And al-Bukhari related from Umm 'Atiyyah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took our pledge at the allegiance that we would not wail. Of us, only five women fulfilled it: Umm Sulaym, Umm al-'Ala', the daughter of Abu Sabrah, the wife of Mu'adh, and two women, or: the daughter of Abu Sabrah, the wife of Mu'adh, and another woman."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1306).]]

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pay attention to the women with this pledge on the day of the Eid, as al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed me that al-Hasan ibn Muslim informed him, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I witnessed the prayer on the day of al-Fitr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman. All of them would pray it before the sermon, then deliver the sermon afterwards. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ came down, and I seem to see him when he seated the men with his hand. Then he proceeded, pushing through them, until he reached the women with Bilal, and said: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you, that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring a slander that they fabricate between their hands and feet...﴾ until he finished the whole verse. Then, when he finished, he said: 'Do you agree to this?' One woman alone answered, and none other responded: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' (Al-Hasan does not know who she was.) He said: 'Then give charity.' He said: Bilal spread out his garment, and the women began throwing in their rings (fatakh) and finger rings into Bilal's garment."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4895).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Sulaym, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "Umaymah bint Ruqayqah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to pledge allegiance to him for Islam. He said: 'I pledge allegiance to you that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your child, nor bring a slander that you fabricate between your hands and your feet, nor wail, nor display your adornment as in the first Jahiliyyah (time of ignorance).'"[[Musnad (2/196).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a gathering, and he said: 'Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your children.' He recited the verse that was taken from the women: ﴿When believing women come to you﴾. 'Whoever of you fulfils it, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of that and is punished for it, it is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of that and Allah conceals it, it is up to Allah: if He wills, He forgives him, and if He wills, He punishes him.'" Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it in their Sahihs.[[Musnad (5/314); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4894); Sahih Muslim, no. (1709).]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Marthad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yazani,[[In manuscript M: "Yazid."]][[In manuscript A: "al-Muzani."]] from Abu 'Abd Allah 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Usaylah al-Sunabihi,[[In manuscript A: "al-Salihi."]] from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: "I was among those who attended the First 'Aqabah. We were twelve men, and we pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the pledge of the women, and that was before war was prescribed: that we would not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor bring a slander that we fabricate between our hands and feet, nor disobey him in what is right." He said: "If you fulfil it, then you will have Paradise." Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Ibn Jarir related, through the route of al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, saying: "Say to them: Indeed the Messenger of Allah pledges allegiance to you that you will not associate anything with Allah." Hind bint 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, who had cut open the belly of Hamzah, was disguised among the women. She said: "If I speak, he will recognise me, and if he recognises me, he will kill me." She disguised herself out of fear of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The women with Hind kept silent and refused to speak. Hind, while still disguised, said: "How can he accept from women something he did not accept from men?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at her, and said to 'Umar: "Say to them: and they will not steal." Hind said: "By Allah, I take some of the wealth of Abu Sufyan, and I do not know whether it is lawful for me or not." Abu Sufyan said: "Whatever you have taken in the past or what remains, it is lawful for you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and recognised her. He called her, and she took hold of his hand and sought refuge with him. He said: "Are you Hind?" She said: "May Allah pardon what has passed." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned from her and said: "And they will not commit adultery." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, does a free woman commit adultery?" He said: "No, by Allah, a free woman does not commit adultery." Then he said: "And they will not kill their children." Hind said: "You killed them on the day of Badr, so you and they know best." He said: ﴿And they will not bring a slander that they fabricate between their hands and feet﴾, and he said: ﴿and they will not disobey you in what is right﴾. He said: He forbade them from wailing. The people of Jahiliyyah used to tear their garments, scratch their faces, cut their hair, and call for destruction (thubur). Thubur means ruin.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/52).]]

This is a strange report (athar), and there is some objectionable content in part of it, and Allah knows best. Abu Sufyan and his wife, when they embraced Islam, were not frightened by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; rather, he showed them purity and affection. Likewise, the matter was from his side towards them, upon him be peace.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was revealed on the day of the Conquest (al-Fath). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pledged allegiance to the men at al-Safa, while 'Umar, on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, pledged allegiance to the women beneath it. He mentioned the rest as it has preceded, and added: When he said ﴿and they will not kill their children﴾, Hind said: "We raised them as children, and you killed them as adults." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab laughed until he fell backwards. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, 'Atiyyah bint Sulayman narrated to me, my paternal aunt narrated to me, from her grandmother,[[In manuscript A: "My paternal uncle narrated to me, from my grandfather."]] from 'A'ishah, who said: "Hind bint 'Utbah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to pledge allegiance to him. He looked at her hand and said: 'Go and change your hand.' She went and changed it with henna, then came back. He said: 'I pledge allegiance to you that you will not associate anything with Allah.' He pledged allegiance to her, and on her hand were two gold bracelets. She said: 'What do you say about these two bracelets?' He said: 'Two embers from the embers of Hell.'"[[Abu Ya'la related it in his Musnad (8/195) from Nasr ibn 'Ali with similar wording, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/37): "In its chain are people whom I do not know."]]

Then, His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you﴾, meaning: whoever of them comes to you pledging allegiance on these conditions, then accept her allegiance. ﴿That they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal﴾, meaning: the property of other people. As for when the husband falls short in providing for her, she may take from his wealth in a reasonable manner what is customary for women like her, even without his knowledge, in accordance with the hadith of Hind bint Utbah, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a stingy man who does not give me enough maintenance to suffice me and my children. Is there any blame on me if I take from his wealth without his knowledge?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take from his wealth in a reasonable manner what suffices you and your children." It was recorded by both of them in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7180) and Sahih Muslim no. (1714).]].

And His saying: ﴿nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse; indeed, it is an immorality and an evil way﴾ [Al-Isra: 32]. The hadith of Samurah mentions the punishment of those who commit adultery with a painful torment in the Blazing Fire [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (5/15).]].

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, who said: Fatimah bint Utbah came to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he took from her: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, and so on, the verse. She said: she placed her hand on her head out of modesty, and he was pleased with what he saw of her. Aishah said: "Stop, O woman, for by Allah, we only pledged allegiance on this." She said: "Yes, then." So he accepted her allegiance on the verse [[al-Musnad (6/151).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Husayn, from Amir, that is al-Sha'bi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge of the women, and there was a garment in his hand which he had placed over his palm. Then he said: "And that they will not kill their children." A woman said: "They kill their fathers and then entrust us with their children?" He said: After that, whenever the women came to pledge allegiance to him, he gathered them and presented this to them; when they affirmed it, they returned.

* *

His saying: ﴿nor kill their children﴾. This includes killing a child after its existence, as the people of the Jahiliyyah used to kill their children out of fear of poverty, and it also includes killing a child while still in the womb, as some ignorant women may do: a woman throws herself down so that she does not conceive, either for a corrupt purpose or something similar.

* *

His saying: ﴿nor bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾. Ibn Abbas said: It means that they should not attribute to their husbands children who are not theirs. Muqatil also said likewise. This is supported by the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud:

Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Amr [meaning Ibn al-Harith] narrated to us, from Ibn al-Hadi, from Abd Allah ibn Yunus, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say when the verse of mutual curse (li'an) was revealed: "Any woman who introduces into a people someone who is not of them, she has nothing to do with Allah, and Allah will never admit her into His Paradise. And any man who denies his child while he is looking at him, Allah will veil Himself from him and expose him before the first and the last [of creation]" [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2263).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿nor disobey you in what is reasonable﴾, meaning: in what you command them of what is reasonable, and what you forbid them of what is evil.

Al-Bukhari said: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Zubayr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿nor disobey you in what is reasonable﴾, he said: "It is only a condition which Allah has imposed upon the women" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4893).]].

Maymun ibn Mihran said: Allah did not make obedience to His Prophet except in what is reasonable, and what is reasonable is obedience.

Ibn Zayd said: Allah commanded obedience to His Messenger, and he is Allah's chosen one among His creation, in what is reasonable. Others besides him have also said, including Ibn Abbas, Anas ibn Malik, Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, Abu Salih, and others: He forbade them that day from wailing (al-niyahah). The hadith of Umm Atiyyah concerning this has already been mentioned earlier as well.

Al-Tabari said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding this verse: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) took from them the pledge not to wail, and not to speak to men except a man of their own who is mahram (unlawful for marriage). Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: "O Prophet of Allah, we have guests, and we are often away from our women." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I did not mean those; I did not mean those" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/51).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Farra' narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, Mubarak narrated to me, from al-Hasan, who said: Among what the Prophet (ﷺ) took [as pledge] was: "Do not speak to men unless she is one who is mahram, for a man keeps talking to a woman until his semen flows between his thighs."

Al-Tabari said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Harun narrated to us, from Amr, from Asim [in M: "from Amr ibn Asim"], from Ibn Sirin, from Umm Atiyyah al-Ansariyyah, who said: Among what was stipulated upon us of what is reasonable when we pledged allegiance was that we should not wail. A woman from Banu Fulan said: "Banu Fulan have helped me, so I must repay them." She went and helped them, then came and pledged allegiance. She said: None of them fulfilled [this pledge] except her and Umm Sulaym bint Milhan, the mother of Anas ibn Malik [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/52).]].

Al-Bukhari also narrated this hadith by way of Hafsah bint Sirin, from Umm Atiyyah Nusaybah al-Ansariyyah, may Allah be pleased with her [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4892).]], and a similar narration has been reported from another route as well.

Al-Tabari said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Umar ibn Farrukh al-Qattat narrated to us, Musab ibn Nuh al-Ansari narrated to me, who said: I met an old woman of ours who was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She said: I came to him to pledge allegiance, and he took from us what he took, that we should not wail. An old woman said: "O Messenger of Allah, some people had helped me in calamities that befell me, and now they have been struck by a calamity, so I want to help them." He said: "Go and repay them." So she went and repaid them, then she came to him and pledged allegiance. She said: This is the reasonable matter which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: ﴿nor disobey you in what is reasonable﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/52).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, al-Qa'nabi [in M: "al-Dabbi"] narrated to us, al-Hajjaj ibn Safwan narrated to us, from Asid [in A: "from Asad"] ibn Abi Asid al-Barrad, from a woman among those who pledged allegiance, who said: Among what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took from us was that we should not disobey him in what is reasonable: that we should not scratch faces, nor loosen our hair, nor tear open our collars, nor call out "woe" [[In M and A: "a face"].].

Al-Tabari said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Yazid, mawla of al-Sahba', from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿nor disobey you in what is reasonable﴾, he said: "Wailing."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in [his book of] Tafsir, from Abd ibn Humayd, from Abu Nu'aym, and Ibn Majah [narrated it] from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Waki', both of them from Yazid ibn Abd Allah al-Shaybani, mawla of al-Sahba', with the same chain [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3307) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1579).]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib.

Al-Tabari said: Muhammad [in M: "Ahmad"] ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Idris narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Uthman Abu Ya'qub narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Atiyyah narrated to me, from his grandmother Umm Atiyyah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived, he gathered the women of the Ansar in a house, then sent Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, to us. He stood at the door and greeted us, and we returned the greeting [or: I returned the greeting], then he said: "I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to you." She said: We said: "Welcome to the Messenger of Allah and the messenger of the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Will you pledge allegiance not to associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse?" She said: We said: "Yes." She said: He extended his hand from outside the door [or: the house], and we extended our hands from inside the house. Then he said: "O Allah, bear witness." She said: He also commanded us, on the two festivals, to bring out the menstruating women and the young unmarried women, and there was no Friday prayer upon us, and he forbade us from following funerals. Isma'il said: I asked my grandmother about His saying: ﴿nor disobey you in what is reasonable﴾, and she said: "Wailing" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/53).]].

In the two Sahihs, through the route of al-A'mash, from Abd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He is not one of us who strikes the cheeks, tears the collars, and calls out with the calls of the Jahiliyyah" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1297) and Sahih Muslim no. (103).]].

Also in the two Sahihs, from Abu Musa: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disavowed the one who raises her voice [in lamentation], the one who shaves her head, and the one who tears her clothes [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1296) and Sahih Muslim no. (104).]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Hudbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Aban ibn Yazid narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, that Zayd narrated to him, that Abu Sallam narrated to him, that Abu Malik al-Ash'ari narrated to him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four [practices] of the matter of the Jahiliyyah remain among my Ummah, which they will not abandon: boasting about lineages, slandering of ancestries, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing." And he said: "The wailing woman, if she does not repent before her death, will be raised on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a coat of mange" [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/148).]].

Muslim recorded it in his Sahih, uniquely, from the hadith of Aban ibn Yazid al-Attar, with the same [chain] [[Sahih Muslim no. (934).]].

And from Abu Sa'id: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the wailing woman and the one who listens to her. Narrated by Abu Dawud [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3128).]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 60, verse 13:

He (may He be blessed and exalted) forbids allegiance to the disbelievers at the end of "this surah" just as He forbade it at its beginning, saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah has been angry﴾, meaning: the Jews, the Christians and all the other disbelievers, those upon whom Allah is angry, whom He has cursed, and who deserve expulsion and distance from Allah. How, then, would you ally with them and take them as friends and intimates, when they have despaired of the Hereafter, that is, of its reward and its bliss in the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? And His saying: ﴿as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾ has two interpretations. The first: as the living disbelievers have despaired of their relatives who are in the graves, of meeting them again after that, because they do not believe in resurrection or raising from the dead, so their hope of them has been cut off by what they believe.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah has been angry﴾ to the end of the surah, meaning: whoever of the disbelievers has died, the living disbelievers have despaired of returning to them or of Allah raising them up, the Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding ﴿as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾: the living disbelievers have despaired of the dead.

Qatadah said: as the disbelievers have despaired that the people of the graves, who have died, would return to them. Likewise said al-Dahhak. Ibn Jarir related them all.

The second statement: its meaning is: as the disbelievers who are in the graves have despaired of every good.

Al-A'mash related from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾ he said: just as this disbeliever has despaired when he dies and witnesses his reward and looks upon it. This is also the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Muqatil, Ibn Zayd, al-Kalbi and Mansur, and it is the preference of Ibn Jarir.
